spec_clauses.spec_clause_text: [STU-UNI-001] ONE DOCUMENT, ONE TOOL SURFACE. Studio presents one unified `StudioDocument` model and one unified tool surface across raster/vector/layout/design-system/whiteboard domains. There are no per-source-app silos: a shared capability exists once as a Studio primitive (14.3) and every operator-facing tool/panel/command is a projection of that single primitive — the same typed contract models call (14.16).

[STU-UNI-005] The operator surface is a control room, not a chat window: it surfaces document/layer state, selection, active tool, pending proposals, validation state, history, and export status as structured state first. It MUST NOT steal keyboard focus or open uncontrolled windows (14.20). --- --- ## 14.22 Studio UserManual (Dual-Audience) Handshake has ONE in-product internal UserManual for no-context models AND operators (CX-982-001). Studio manual coverage MUST be extensive and dual-audience. This sub-section is normative and binds to HBR-MAN.

[STU-MDL-002] FRONTEND VISIBILITY. Every operator-visible Studio surface (pane, panel, tab, tool, control, canvas) MUST expose a stable `author_id` target through the native AccessKit/egui accessibility tree so Argus can identify, inspect, and steer it. The frontend MUST expose machine-readable UI-state snapshots (which tool is active, current selection, panel/layout state, document/artboard focus) queryable without pixel screen-reading.

[STU-QUIET-003] NON-INTRUSIVE CO-WORK. While the operator uses Studio (or any other Handshake module) on a project/module, agent work on a different project/module MUST NOT bring Studio to the foreground, pop panes, move the operator's viewport, or change the operator's active tool/selection. Agent activity in the operator's current file is surfaced through presence/pending-proposal indicators (14.21), never through intrusive UI takeover.

implementation_notes.naming: Vendor product names are provenance only. Studio ships Handshake-native names per [STU-SECTION-003].
implementation_notes.database: SurrealDB with the EventLedger is the only durable authority. SQLite, libSQL, Turso and PostgreSQL are forbidden, including in tests and dev caches.
implementation_notes.engine_split: GPU, WGSL and compute live in the studio-engine crate behind its traits. handshake_core must never gain a GPU dependency.
implementation_notes.routing: Navigation extends the existing address and bus seams. No new router.
implementation_notes.worktree: Code paths resolve against the WP-KERNEL-012 worktree, never main.

spec_clauses.spec_clause_text: [STU-UNI-001] ONE DOCUMENT, ONE TOOL SURFACE. Studio presents one unified `StudioDocument` model and one unified tool surface across raster/vector/layout/design-system/whiteboard domains. There are no per-source-app silos: a shared capability exists once as a Studio primitive (14.3) and every operator-facing tool/panel/command is a projection of that single primitive — the same typed contract models call (14.16).

[STU-UNI-005] The operator surface is a control room, not a chat window: it surfaces document/layer state, selection, active tool, pending proposals, validation state, history, and export status as structured state first. It MUST NOT steal keyboard focus or open uncontrolled windows (14.20). --- --- ## 14.22 Studio UserManual (Dual-Audience) Handshake has ONE in-product internal UserManual for no-context models AND operators (CX-982-001). Studio manual coverage MUST be extensive and dual-audience. This sub-section is normative and binds to HBR-MAN.

[STU-MDL-002] FRONTEND VISIBILITY.
